title: Coarse-graining to create minimalist models for dynamic, end-linked star-polymer networks
authors: Tyla R. Holoman, C. Levi Petix, Michael P. Howard, Thomas M. Truskett
abstract: Although minimalist models for patchy attractive particles have revealed powerful design rules for how particle valence directs colloidal assembly, less work has focused on comparably simple models of reversible, network-forming star polymers. Here, we use relative-entropy coarse-graining and simulation results from finer-resolution bead--spring star polymers to generate 5-bead models of dynamic, end-associating four-armed poly(ethylene glycol) macromers. Our results comparing structural correlations, network connectivity, and phase behavior of the coarse- and fine-grained models provide insight into how the accuracy and transferability of the coarse-grained models depend on the state point chosen for coarse-graining. The results also reveal intrinsic trade-offs between reducing degrees of freedom and expanding the range of effective interactions in coarse-graining that impact the total number of pairwise interactions in the resulting model, with implications for its computational efficiency.
summary: This work develops a coarse-grained model for dynamic star-polymer networks by mapping a detailed bead-spring simulation onto a much simpler 5-bead model using relative-entropy minimization. The authors demonstrate that the simplified model accurately predicts key structural and phase behaviors of the complex system across different concentrations. This research highlights the fundamental trade-offs inherent in multiscale modeling, balancing computational efficiency against physical accuracy.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop and validate minimalist, coarse-grained models for complex, dynamic star-polymer networks to predict their macroscopic behavior while managing the trade-off between model simplicity and accuracy.
main_result: The coarse-grained model successfully reproduces the structural correlations and phase behavior of the fine-grained model across various densities, demonstrating the transferability of the mapping.
method: The study employs relative-entropy coarse-graining, minimizing the relative entropy between the fine-grained and coarse-grained ensembles to derive effective parameters for the simplified model.
model_or_system: The system consists of dynamic, end-associating four-armed poly(ethylene glycol) (tetra-PEG) macromers forming gel networks. Two models are compared: a detailed bead-spring (fine-grained) model and a simplified 5-bead (coarse-grained) model.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical system and the need for simplification. It details the relative-entropy coarse-graining methodology, followed by simulations comparing the two model types across different densities. The discussion focuses on the resulting trade-offs between model complexity and predictive power.
why_interesting: While focused on classical polymer physics, the rigorous application of relative entropy and the systematic reduction of degrees of freedom mirrors techniques used in developing effective Hamiltonians in quantum many-body systems, which is relevant for understanding complex quantum dynamics.
